edits.old: MongoDB's v8.0 `serverStatus` documentation lists `numBucketsClosedDueToMemoryThreshold` and `numBucketsClosedDueToCachePressure` as separate bucket-catalog fields. SERVER-89233 reports the cache-pressure counter, while a 2026 deployment report gives the memory-threshold counter. Those reports do not establish that the counters are interchangeable; compare each using the definition for the deployed server release. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-16)
edits.new: MongoDB's v8.0 `serverStatus` documentation lists `numBucketsClosedDueToMemoryThreshold` and `numBucketsClosedDueToCachePressure` as separate bucket-catalog fields with different definitions: the first counts buckets closed because the set of active buckets did not fit within the allowed bucket catalog cache size, the second counts buckets closed because their size exceeded the dynamic, cache-derived bucket size limit. SERVER-89233 reports the cache-pressure counter. The counters are not interchangeable; compare each using the definition for the deployed server release. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/reference/command/serverStatus.md ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-89233

edits.old: MongoDB v8.0 sets the ordinary bucket cap at 1,000 measurements or 125KB, whichever is lower, and says high-cardinality workloads may receive a lower cap so the bucket working set fits in WiredTiger cache. A MongoDB Community load-test report illustrates the fragmentation risk: a Type 2 chunk loaded after work in other collections produced 420,000 buckets, one average measurement per commit, and 415,000 cache-pressure closures; loading the chunk first produced 25,000 buckets and 17 average measurements per commit. The poster reported at least three times more space in the fragmented run. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

evidence.quote: The new section gives some clues that the optimization and salient metrics to watch have to do with buckets, their management in terms of “opening” and “closing” them with respect to aspects such as the metadata, the number of items, the total size of the bucket, the time boundaries, as well as memory pressure.
| `numBucketsClosedDueToMemoryThreshold` | The number of buckets closed because the set of active buckets didn't fit within the allowed bucket catalog cache size. |

| `numBucketsClosedDueToCachePressure` | The number of buckets closed because their size exceeds the bucket catalog's dynamic [bucket size limit](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md#std-label-timeseries-bucket-closure) derived from available storage engine cache size and `numBuckets`. This limit is distinct from the maximum bucket size limit. |

edits.rationale: In the July 2021 +N Consulting blog walkthrough of time-series collections, the author demonstrated db.sensings.stats().timeseries showing bucket closure counters including memory threshold, time forward, count, and size, noting they had no insight into interpreting them. MongoDB documentation for serverStatus (v8.0) explicitly documents distinct definitions for numBucketsClosedDueToMemoryThreshold (exceeding bucket catalog cache size) and numBucketsClosedDueToCachePressure (derived from available storage engine cache and bucket count).
